meta.title: System Design Roadmap for Beginners | Parmeshwar Metkar posted on the topic | LinkedIn
meta.description:
🚀 Want to learn System Design but don’t know where to start?

Don’t jump straight into designing WhatsApp, Zomato, or Netflix.

First, build the foundation. 🧠

Here’s a practical System Design Roadmap:

🔹 Phase 1 — Networking Basics
• How the Internet works
• TCP vs UDP
• HTTP/HTTPS & TLS
• DNS Resolution
• REST APIs

🔹 Phase 2 — Core Building Blocks
• Load Balancers
• CDN
• Redis & Caching
• API Gateway
• SQL vs NoSQL
• Kafka & Message Queues

🔹 Phase 3 — Patterns & Concepts
• CAP Theorem
• Consistent Hashing
• Database Sharding
• Idempotency
• Outbox Pattern
• Saga & CQRS
• Rate Limiting

🔹 Phase 4 — Real-World Design
• URL Shortener
• Chat System
• Food Delivery App
• Notification System
• Rate Limiter

💡 The biggest mistake?
Trying to solve complex system-design problems before understanding the fundamentals.

Build the foundation → Learn the building blocks → Understand the patterns → Design real systems.

Save this roadmap 📌 and use it as your System Design learning checklist.

#SystemDesign #SoftwareEngineering #BackendDevelopment #DistributedSystems #SoftwareDeveloper #Coding #TechCareer

Kelvorn on Instagram: "Reverse proxies aren't just "traffic routers." The real signal is in 4 metrics:

⏱️ Latency — time for one request to make a round trip
📊 Throughput — how many requests get handled per second
📶 Bandwidth — the max data capacity of the link itself
📈 Jitter — how consistent that delay actually is, request to request

Most setups look fine on paper until jitter spikes under real traffic — that's usually where things quietly fall apart.

Which one do you check first when an API feels "slow"?

#systemdesign #softwarearchitecture #backendengineering #distributedsystems #apidesign"
